title: One Mountain, Many Names
logline: Pilgrims of different faiths climb through the night to the same summit. Each calls it by a different name, and at dawn they all stand in front of the same stone, wind and light.
human_question: When many people call one thing by different names, what are they all looking at?

premise.story: A night climb with pilgrims whose words for the mountain, the mark at its summit, and the journey itself differ by language and faith, while their steps, breath and cold are shared.
premise.place: A sacred mountain known by several names in several traditions.
premise.experience: The viewer climbs in the dark through names, chants and stories, and arrives at a summit where, for a moment, only light, wind and stone are there.

concept_links.why: Several name-concepts for one collective whole; sound, name and meaning separated in real use.
Conventional truth (the many names) alongside what remains when the names fall silent at dawn.
From the summit, the whole land is visible at once, like the full map of the mind seen in one view before the series walks through it.

what_camera_could_observe: Pilgrims of different backgrounds greeting each other on the steps
Chants and calls in several languages
Hands on railings, breath in cold air, lamps along the path
The summit at sunrise; the mountain's shadow if it appears
From the summit, the whole landscape laid out at once: the map before the journey
what_must_be_real: The pilgrims, their words and their reasons. No staged interfaith moments.

possible_arc.opening: Night, lamps, many languages on one path.
possible_arc.turn: The climb strips everyone down to breath and effort.
possible_arc.ending_open: Dawn at the summit. Whatever people actually do and say there leads the ending.

position_hint: opening candidate: a strong first film for Group 1 and a natural Object 1 acquisition moment, if one really happens

requirements: A single place genuinely named differently by different communities
Night and dawn access; safe filming on steps
Pilgrims willing to speak about the names they use

suggestions.name: Sri Pada / Adam's Peak (Samanalakanda, Sivanolipatha Malai)
suggestions.why: One mountain held sacred by Buddhist, Hindu, Muslim and Christian pilgrims, each with its own name and story.
suggestions.season_notes: Pilgrim season, roughly Unduvap Poya (Dec) to Vesak (May)
suggestions.access_notes: Crowded on poya weekends; Hatton (Nallathanni) and Ratnapura (Palabaddala) routes
suggestions.verify: Access, permissions and current conditions are unverified.

risks: Religious sensitivity: never rank or contrast faiths
drop_if: Pilgrims do not actually use different names in practice

connections.note: A concrete, filmable form of the pilot 'The Name in Use'.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
